newsitem.title: USA: Release of Arkansas rapist ignites political furor.
newsitem.headline: Release of Arkansas rapist ignites political furor.

text.p: A political furore raged in Arkansas Friday one day after the state parole board voted to release a criminal serving a life sentence for the rape of President Clinton's cousin.

State law required Gov. Mike Huckabee to declare by Sunday if he would commute Wayne Dumond's sentence. The Parole Board's action relieved Huckabee of the decision, although he termed the Board's action "justifiable and responsible."

But several women members took the floor of the Arkansas House of Representative Friday morning to condemn the parole in addresses so emotional they could barely speak. The state representative whose district includes the victim's home town introduced a resolution calling for a legislative investigation of the parole.
The rape occurred in 1984 while Clinton was governor. Clinton denied Dumond executive clemency, but his successor, Jim Guy Tucker, reduced Dumond's sentence, making him eligible for parole.

Dumond and his supporters have long accused Clinton of undermining Dumond's parole applications because of Clinton's relationship to the victim, a charge that Clinton consistently denied, saying he and his cousin had rarely seen one another.
Asked Friday if he believed that Clinton had influenced the parole board against Dumond, Huckabee replied: "The only person in the whole world who could answer that would be Bill Clinton."

Huckabee came under intense criticism from women's groups and the victim last year when he said he was considering setting Dumond free. Huckabee said Dumond had already served a longer sentence than others convicted of rape, and noted that Dumond had been castrated by unidentified vigilantes while free on bond awaiting trial.

Huckabee said he took no "official action" regarding Dumond's parole. He said he "welcomed" a legislative probe of his handling of the case but said it was only fair to also question his two predecessors.
"Since this case involved three governors, all three should be asked to explain any contact that they may have had with the case," Huckabee said.
Huckabee, who was lieutenant governor, became governor last year when Tucker resigned following his conviction in a Whitewater-related case.
